reading.ours: two units of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — an instrument check, and it is printed first because nothing below it means anything until it passes. The true ratio is a little UNDER 2: both sides pay the driving loop once, so the exact expectation is (2u + L) / (u + L) with L the loop and u one unit, which at sixteen dependent steps per unit puts it around 1.9. A reading below 1.5 means this process could not resolve a deliberate doubling, and the runner voids the report rather than printing prices under it.

reading.ours: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: the same body again, over its own copy of the same state
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — the noise floor. The two sides are identical code over identical, separately-allocated state, so the true ratio is 1.00 exactly and every departure from it printed here was produced by this machine at this moment. The rule that follows is the one the whole table is read under: NO RATIO CLOSER TO 1.00 THAN THIS GAP IS A READING. It also bounds the per-row noise figure, which is the same idea measured again inside every pair — each pair times its floor twice, once before our side and once after, and prints how far the two disagreed.

reading.ours: one member of a bucket of 100 is written and the bucket is read — settled by reposition
reading.floor: the same write and the same read, settled by sorting the whole bucket
reading.caveat: A BUCKET OF 100, and the size is in the id because the answer depends on it: the repair is one scan plus two splices plus a binary search where the sort is a pass over everything, so a single size would be a pair that picked its own answer. Every operation is one row's sort column written, one frame closed, and one bucket read — the read is where an order is settled, on both designs. WHAT THE FULL RE-SORT BUYS is everything `membersInOrder` is: the budget arithmetic that decides when repairing one member at a time has stopped being cheaper than sorting, the reproduction of `Array.prototype.sort`'s stable tie-breaking so a member reported moved whose key did not move goes back exactly where it sat, the two rescue paths that put movers back when the caller's comparator throws with them spliced out of the list, and the walk that spots a bulk load which arrived already in order. Five hundred lines against three, and the three cannot be got wrong. DIRECTION, three ways, and two of them are ours: (1) the write, the frame and the read call are IDENTICAL on both halves and are inside both numbers, which pulls this ratio toward 1.00 — the settle-only difference is larger than this row shows, and that is most of the distance between this row and the 13x/22x/26x our own notes remember for the settle alone; (2) the floor keeps neither a newcomers list nor a movers list, so the write-side bookkeeping our design pays for is charged to us and to nothing on the other side; (3) against those, the floor is NOT charged for the one thing a sort cannot answer — whether the order actually CHANGED. Ours computes it as a by-product (a mover's landing against where it sat) and the engine wakes a subscriber only when it says yes; the floor would need a copy of the list and a walk of it, and since nothing here subscribes to these buckets it never pays for one. That flatters the floor.

reading.ours: the bucket is on the slot and carries its key — one === and no lookup
reading.floor: recompute, recall from a Map, and diff the two through a pair of Sets
reading.caveat: THE DESIGN THIS ONE REPLACED, and the reason the fix was to make the eager recompute cheap rather than to make it lazy: what cost 174 ns was not "index work", it was two allocations and a hash on a path that had already decided nothing needed to move. The diff BUYS cardinality-independence — one body serves one address and fifty, so the two membership sources this package ships would have been one class. EVERY OPERATION IS ONE ROW WRITTEN AND ONE ROW RE-FILED, and the address never moves: the selector reads two columns, the write moves the one that does not decide the address, and the index recomputes the group the row already sits in. That is the ordinary case for any address derived from more than one column, and it is where the three designs differ. DIRECTION: the write, the mark, the delta and the frame are identical on both halves and are inside both numbers, so this ratio is pulled hard toward 1.00 — the per-filing difference our own notes remember (174.1 against 34.8 against 7.5 ns) was measured on the filing alone and is necessarily wider than what this row prints. Two things flatter the FLOOR and are stated so nobody has to find them: it is handed the row's index cell to find the bucket it reports on, which its own design would have resolved with another lookup; and the `Map` of one entry per row that it keeps alive — memory our design does not spend at all, because the answer rides on the row — is in neither number.

reading.ours: the bucket is on the slot and carries its key — one === and no lookup
reading.floor: the same one ===, against a key recalled from a Map keyed by the row
reading.caveat: THE MIDDLE ARM, and the one that isolates the claim. The allocations are gone and the comparison is the same comparison; all that is left between this floor and ours is WHERE the previous answer was kept — in a hash table beside the population, or in a cell on the row itself. That is the identity principle priced directly, and it is the number to quote for it rather than the row above, which also carries the diff's allocations. What the Map BUYS is that the row keeps nothing: a membership can be maintained for rows this index does not own, and no cell is reserved on every row of the population for an index most rows may never be read through. reading.ours: re-file a row under 2 addresses — two linear scans through the store's own comparison
reading.floor: the same re-file, diffed through a Set of the 2 keys
reading.caveat: 2 ADDRESSES PER ROW. Ours is O(A²) word comparisons and no allocation; the floor is O(A) with two `Set`s allocated per write. THE CROSSOVER IS THE CLAIM this family exists to check, and it is the one thing the shared cost cannot distort: the write, the frame and the selector are identical on both halves, so they add the same constant to both numbers — which pulls each RATIO toward 1.00 but leaves the size at which the two designs are equal exactly where it was. Read the family, not the row. WHAT THE SET BUYS is that it does not degrade: at some size the scans lose and keep losing. WHAT IT GIVES UP is not nanoseconds — the scans ask the STORE whether a bucket is addressed by a key, so an index filed by a chain of identities is served by the shipped design and cannot be served by this floor at all, which is why this floor is writable only over a keyed store. Every timed operation leaves the address list unchanged, which is the steady state both designs are written for; the floor delegates the leaves and the joins of a CHANGED list to the shipped code, and no timed operation takes that branch.
